statements.title: Undisclosed implementation choices
statements.speaker: Manu Seyfzadeh
statements.paraphrase: He filled gaps experimentally for sub-aperture synthesis, registration and depth focusing. He describes his own implementation.

statements.title: Fixed half-band reference
statements.speaker: Manu Seyfzadeh
statements.location: Human prompt following the band-pass filter design question
statements.paraphrase: He proposes a fixed half-band master and many partly overlapping half-band copies.
statements.basis: Written prompt by Seyfzadeh; his technical interpretation, no Biondi confirmation

statements.title: Suggested 1-100 Hz range
statements.speaker: Manu Seyfzadeh
statements.location: Human question about whether seismic frequencies between 1 and 100 Hz are plausible
statements.paraphrase: He asks if 1-100 Hz could be the band for seismic frequencies. ChatGPT agrees.
statements.basis: Written question by Seyfzadeh; model answer excluded

statements.title: Interpreting a surface ellipse
statements.speaker: Manu Seyfzadeh
statements.paraphrase: He describes a surface ellipse from vertical and transverse oscillation as his interpretation, drawing on an external geophysicist.

statements.title: Pairing two displaced looks
statements.speaker: Manu Seyfzadeh
statements.paraphrase: He uses a single flyover, many Doppler sub-apertures, and slightly displaced reference and offset copies within each one.

statements.title: Focusing against candidate depths
statements.speaker: Manu Seyfzadeh
statements.paraphrase: He describes an adjoint focusing operator against theoretical phase histories for candidate depths. Biondi asks about the displacement matrix.

statements.title: Encoding vibration direction
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He proposes extending the display to encode horizontal, vertical and oblique vibration orientation using a second polarimetry patent.

statements.title: Choosing the section direction
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: Biondi recommends a range-oriented section. He describes lower quality when the line and sub-aperture split are both in azimuth.

statements.title: Coarse and fine registration windows
statements.speaker: Manu Seyfzadeh
statements.paraphrase: His coarse registration frame is 128 by 128 pixels. The fine frame is 24 azimuth by 32 range pixels. He tested recovery with injected vectors.

statements.title: Converting pixel shifts to metres
statements.speaker: Manu Seyfzadeh
statements.paraphrase: He converts range and azimuth pixel scales independently to metres from delivered metadata.

statements.title: Calibrating the rock-speed model
statements.speaker: Manu Seyfzadeh
statements.paraphrase: He says he changed the rock-speed model, calibrated with Campbell’s Tomb and a shaft by Khufu, then applied the derived rule to Osiris.

statements.title: Choosing the wavelength
statements.speaker: Manu Seyfzadeh
statements.paraphrase: He says he used a different wavelength from 0.24 m and again cites calibration at Campbell’s Tomb.

statements.title: Uncertainty in the depth estimate
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: Reviewing the Khafre similarity, Biondi says the depth estimate still needs work.

statements.title: Changing the sub-aperture count
statements.speaker: Seyfzadeh, then Biondi
statements.paraphrase: Seyfzadeh says K was 295. Biondi suggests trying 5000 after seeing the output.

statements.title: Version and filter changes
statements.speaker: Trevor Grassi
statements.paraphrase: He distinguishes a first Osiris output, a 100 m version described as 3360 pixels, and a later version with stronger filtering.

statements.title: Aligning output with a drawing
statements.speaker: Trevor Grassi
statements.paraphrase: He marked corresponding spots in Photoshop and discusses matching a perspective drawing to a different section view.

statements.title: First tests with a Capella image
statements.speaker: Manu Seyfzadeh
statements.paraphrase: Initial Giza tests used a lower-resolution image supplied without charge by Capella.

statements.title: Sharing an image and a line
statements.speaker: Manu Seyfzadeh
statements.paraphrase: He says a placement line was sent to Biondi and both had access to the image from Athanatos.

statements.title: Confidence in the Osiris identification
statements.speaker: Manu Seyfzadeh
statements.paraphrase: His expressed confidence in seeing Osiris is above 50 percent and below 100 percent at this point.

statements.title: Horizontal mismatch in the Khufu overlay
statements.speaker: Trevor Grassi
statements.paraphrase: In his Khufu overlay, Grassi asks viewers to compare chamber heights and notes the horizontal mismatch.

statements.title: Doppler bandwidth and half-band scanning
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He describes spotlight Doppler bandwidths of roughly 22-25 kHz and using half the available band to scan along the aperture. He separately mentions a roughly 10 GHz carrier.

statements.title: Moving processing to GPUs
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: Biondi says they optimized the kernel and were moving towards GPU processing while retaining the same technique.

statements.title: Retuning the method for depth
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He says they tuned the software differently once the aim changed from the top of the pyramid to deeper targets.

statements.title: Averaging several Gran Sasso sections
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: For the wide Gran Sasso target he describes wider focusing and averaging several lines pixel by pixel to reduce noise. He reports at least two months of processing.

statements.title: Discarding noise-dominated outputs
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He says they discarded many trials where noise was inverted and kept successes. He mentions hundreds of successes on other things.

statements.title: MATLAB to CUDA processing times
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He describes the Gran Sasso demonstration as software 1.0, a MATLAB to C++/CUDA rewrite, and a change from about a month to three or four hours.

statements.title: Coherent processing of complex returns
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He says the processing is coherent and handles real and imaginary components. It uses an aperture of displaced measurements to infer direction.

statements.title: A three-band colour image
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He describes a colour Capella image made from three Doppler bands.

statements.title: Pseudo-inversion and the role of AI
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He says the model is pseudo-inverted, reports four providers and distinguishes that reconstruction from AI.

statements.title: Limits of spiral interpretation
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He describes the spiral as a shape. He cannot distinguish stairs from cables and describes material recognition as future work requiring ground truth.

statements.title: Depth depends on the local geology
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He says accurate depth needs the local geological model and constant density produces only a rough estimate.

statements.title: Unscaled depth axis in the spiral model
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: Biondi says the displayed spiral model has an unscaled depth axis. He says in-person examination would distinguish what the apparent spiral represents.

statements.title: Reading 648 m from a displayed ratio
statements.speaker: Khafre Project speaker at Bologna (Italian release)
statements.paraphrase: The presentation explicitly counts pixels relative to the 137 m height of Khafre and reads 648 m to the end platform. The speaker acknowledges obliquity and argues that the angular errors cancel in the ratio.

statements.title: A visible cutoff and deeper estimates
statements.speaker: Mixed panel; speaker changes in captions
statements.paraphrase: The panel discusses a visible cutoff near 550-600 m and questions a deeper estimate. Attribution changes during the exchange.

statements.title: Claim to have measured the Big Void
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He says their model contains the Big Void and they measured its dimensions.

statements.title: Separating Big Void and corridor priority
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: The conversation identifies Big Void on a slide. Biondi associates his six-month priority claim with the corridor in the following sentences.

statements.title: Claimed orientation of the Big Void
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He tells Matt Beall that they detected the Big Void and offers a different orientation from the Grand Gallery.

statements.title: Selecting the second-Sphinx search area
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He describes selecting the second Sphinx location after Damiano Piras and others suggested that area.

statements.title: Compute requirements in meeting footage
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: In edited meeting footage, he describes using multiple cores and needing more computing capacity.

statements.title: An unspecified stage in the 2022 paper
statements.speaker: Manu Seyfzadeh
statements.paraphrase: In his 2022 reading of the paper, he notes that he could not find a detailed explanation of one stage. This predates his later reconstruction.

statements.title: Carlin Tunnel as a proposed example
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.location: Post text, Carlin Tunnel railway, Nevada
statements.paraphrase: He describes deep geocoding with one SLC and names the Carlin railway tunnel as an example.

statements.title: Program claims and intended external review
statements.speaker: Grassi and Frank Rogala
statements.location: Initial report, abstract and project introduction
statements.paraphrase: The program attributes deep imaging and material identification to the software and describes a proposed third-party check under NDA.

statements.title: Eight shafts and two large chambers
statements.speaker: Khafre Project (three signatories)
statements.paraphrase: The signed abstract describes eight shafts, two rows, 648 m depth and two cubes of approximately 80 m per side. It credits Capella and Umbra and multiple tomograms.

statements.title: Tracking the Doppler centroid
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He says changing surface motion shifts the estimated Doppler centroid. He records its history and attempts the inversion from it.

statements.title: Vegetation as a source of noise
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: Biondi expects dense vegetation to add noise and says he has not tested strongly vegetated terrain.

statements.title: Expected brightness of chamber edges
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He says air inside a chamber should appear dark and its borders bright in his tomogram.

statements.title: Extracting a section between two pixels
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He says to select two image pixels, draw a line and extract a vertical section.

statements.title: Repeated Fourier transforms and runtime
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He describes calculating shifts with repeated FFTs and inverse FFTs over a large data region. He gives roughly two weeks of continuous processing for the example.

statements.title: Proposed tests on the ground
statements.speaker: Filippo Biondi
statements.paraphrase: He proposes ground radar and seismic/electrical methods to validate the satellite work. The phrasing is future tense.

statements.title: Malanga’s proposed independent review
statements.speaker: Counsel speaking for Corrado Malanga
statements.paraphrase: The letter describes the method as SAR Doppler tomography and multichromatic analysis of micro-motion. It announces plans for an independent review of the data and processing chain.
statements.basis: Written statement on behalf of Malanga; paraphrased

repositories.name: teoAmico/ResonarSat
repositories.qualification: Examined the source and constants. No new full-scene Giza run.

repositories.name: mfwarren/Pyramid
repositories.scope: Independent Sentinel-1 IW TOPS Giza experiments.
repositories.qualification: Code and result JSON are public. Its explicit sensor and geometry choices differ from the Giza spotlight claims.

repositories.name: Hassanforeman/subsurface-sar-tomo
repositories.scope: Independent controls-first tracker and depth-operator analysis.
repositories.qualification: Executed the deterministic expected-power routine and checked its answer using independent QR and impulse propagation. Its null applies to accumulated and detrended noise.

repositories.name: not-JASH/sar-doppler-tomography
repositories.scope: Independent CUDA chain and observation-space benchmark.
repositories.qualification: Optional one-sided filtering encodes a sign convention. Blind recovery of physical polarity would need signed ground truth. The benchmark supplies its own forward-model observations.

repositories.name: simossss/sar-tomography-reproduction
repositories.scope: Independent Umbra single-pass surrogate plus separate Sentinel-1 multi-pass test.
repositories.qualification: The single-pass branch averages reconstructed complex values per subband. Its scores test a different observable from paired displacement.

repositories.name: emmanuel6474/biondirepro
repositories.scope: Independent Vesuvius operator and published-figure audit.
repositories.qualification: Useful control designs and source-fidelity checks. This is not Biondi’s processing source or a sensor-to-cavity validation.

repositories.name: juanvillaverde/harmonicsar
repositories.qualification: The only JavaScript file in this revision runs the web interface and canvas illustration.
